## Glossary

**addLogBroadcast**  
Also sends every log call in the current async scope to an extra target.

**configFromSaved**  
Saved settings.json to full config over defaults, migrating legacy `providers` to `vendors`.

**ConfigRevisionError**  
Thrown when settings changed elsewhere since they were read: reload before saving.

**ConfigStore**  
Persists settings to disk with JSON patch semantics and revisions; the viewer reads and writes through it.

**database**  
Class: Postgres via Prisma (schema, db scripts, JSON helpers) and Redis.

**defaultConfig / starterConfig / defaultAgents**  
Full defaults / minimal first-install bootstrap / the one bare executor.

**enqueueJob**  
The only way to put work on the queue: handler name plus typed payload.

**foundry-jobs**  
The BullMQ queue on Redis that background jobs run on.

**.foundry/audit.jsonl**  
Audit log: a before/after row per committed settings change (`GET /api/settings/history`).

**.foundry/project.json**  
A repository's committed project settings (e.g. `chorus`); machine settings win key by key.

**.foundry/settings.json**  
Runtime config: default provider/model, vendors, agents, composition, layers, sources, projects.

**foundry_test**  
The local test database: `bun run db:push:test` then `bun run test:db`.

**installationName**  
This Foundry's name, used by Kingdom pairing.

**jobs**  
Class: BullMQ queue on Redis, makeJob / makeSingletonJob, worker, handlers.

**journal.rawMiddlewareDays**  
Retention days for raw middleware journal rows (default 30).

**logger**  
Class: pluggable logger (consola, pino) with async scopes.

**logScope**  
Runs a function so every log inside carries a named, nestable scope tag.

**makeSingletonJob**  
A job handler superseded when a newer run is queued (SupersededError).

**Prisma schema**  
`prisma/schema.prisma`: Entry, Trace, Span, Signal, Intervention, ThreadState, Message; Postgres with pgvector.

**projects[id].agents**  
Project agents: standalone or `extends: <global id>` with optional `override`; never Wardens.

**refuseHandNamedWardens**  
Refuses domain-advising, domain-librarian or decider agents in settings by name, with the fix.

**registerConfigValidator**  
Adds a check that runs on every validateConfig.

**settings**  
Class: the settings model: .foundry/settings.json, ConfigStore with patch semantics and revisions, resolution, settings routes.

**toPrismaJson**  
Converts a value for a Prisma JSON column (null becomes JsonNull); toOptionalPrismaJson leaves undefined unset.

**unwrapped**  
A thread with no layers, classifier, router, Cartographer or thread-state: the fresh-install default (wrapsThread).

**validateConfig**  
Validates a full config, rejecting retired keys and running registered validators.

**vendors**  
Settings key: each vendor on/off with a subscription mode and an API mode.

**warmLayers**  
Singleton job that warms all context layers in a thread's stack.

## 1. What this Warden covers

The settings model (`.foundry/settings.json`, how it is loaded over defaults, validated, saved with patch semantics and applied live) and the runtime plumbing underneath Foundry: the BullMQ job queue, the scoped logger, and Postgres through Prisma.

## 2. The domain

The `settings` class owns `.foundry/settings.json`. ConfigStore is the only writer: it persists with JSON patch semantics and revisions (a stale write raises ConfigRevisionError), and every committed change becomes a before/after row in `.foundry/audit.jsonl` (`GET /api/settings/history`, settingsChanges computes the per-definition diff); running threads take edited layers, agents and instructions on their next turn, while region, chorus-enable and provider changes apply to new threads. configFromSaved turns the saved file into a full config over defaults and migrates pre-vendor `providers` to `vendors`; validateConfig rejects retired keys and runs the checks added with registerConfigValidator. For defaults choose by scope: defaultConfig is the full default config, starterConfig the minimal first-install bootstrap for a chosen provider and model, defaultAgents just the one bare executor; a fresh install is unwrapped (wrapsThread) and everything else is opt-in. readRepositorySettings reads a repository's committed `.foundry/project.json` raw, reporting malformed files instead of throwing. Project agents (`projects[id].agents`) are standalone or `extends: <global agent id>` with `override`, and are never Wardens: hand-named domain-advising, domain-librarian or decider agents are refused by name. On the viewer side loadSettings fills the settingsConfig signal and the control, models and runtime route folders serve the settings endpoints.

The runtime classes are small. `jobs`: enqueueJob is the only way onto the `foundry-jobs` queue (createQueue, on its own Redis connection; initializeWorker processes it); define handlers with makeJob when every payload must run, makeSingletonJob when a newer run should supersede an older one (warmLayers is one). `logger`: createConsolaLogger for human-read dev and CLI output, createPinoLogger for structured JSON lines; logScope tags everything inside a function with a named, nestable scope (names in LogScope), addLogBroadcast copies a scope's log calls to an extra target. `database`: the Prisma schema (Entry, Trace, Span, Signal, Intervention, ThreadState, Message on Postgres with pgvector), `bun run db:push` for the configured database, `db:push:test` then `test:db` for the local `foundry_test` database. The tech stack is fixed: Bun, strict TypeScript, bun test, BullMQ, Prisma/Postgres, SQLite for the local session store.

Many part-3 doc members are settings keys whose behaviour lives in another region; point there for the behaviour: `chorus.layers`, the warm-cache key and hand-named Warden refusal are `chorus`; `@inixiative/foundry/classify` and charters are `classify`; the composition view is `composition`; source versions and CompositionAuditor.recompose are `audit-log`; subagent child threads, middleware-reduced rows and the journal are `threads-journal`; the vendors registry is `models-providers`; the archive capture claim is `archive`. Not here: installing the daemon, doctor, `bun run setup` and last-good settings are `install-daemon`; the viewer's settings pages and server are `viewer`; test tiers other than `test:db` are `testing-vcr`.

### Class `jobs`: BullMQ queue on Redis, makeJob / makeSingletonJob, worker, handlers

**Job: define a background job handler** (makeJob vs makeSingletonJob) — catalog choose lines (packages/foundry/src/jobs/)

*Said as:* "run this in the background", "only the latest run should survive", "don't let two cleanups overlap"

| Member | Use when | Not when (use instead) |
|---|---|---|
| **makeJob** | every payload must run | overlap is waste and only the latest matters (use makeSingletonJob) |
| **makeSingletonJob** | periodic or idempotent work; a newer run supersedes the older | every payload must run (use makeJob) |
| **warmLayers** | the existing singleton that warms a thread's layers | a new kind of job (define with makeJob or makeSingletonJob) |

| **createQueue** | create the BullMQ queue on its own Redis connection | adding work (use enqueueJob) |
| **initializeWorker** | start the worker that processes foundry-jobs | adding work (use enqueueJob) |

### Class `database`: Postgres via Prisma (schema, db scripts, JSON helpers) and Redis

## 4. The specifics, in full

### 4a. Doc sections

Each unit is the doc section verbatim, with its headings shifted down two levels. A source line above it gives the path, the section and the doc's H1.

<!-- unit doc:CLAUDE.md#config -->
**Source:** `CLAUDE.md` § Config (in "Foundry")

#### Config

Runtime config lives in `.foundry/settings.json`. A fresh install is one executor (`defaultAgents`: no instructions, inheriting the default provider and model) and nothing else, so its threads are **unwrapped**: no layers, classifier, router, Cartographer call or thread-state reach the native session (`wrapsThread` in `agents/thread-runtime.ts`). Everything below is opt-in. The old starter stack (system / conventions / memory layers, classifier → router → prompt-only executors) is flagged by `bun run doctor` and removed by `bun run setup --remove-legacy-defaults` when unedited (`setup/legacy-starter.ts`). Foundry's own signals are written into the memory store only while a configured `file` source reads it.

It defines:
- Default provider/model
- Vendors (`vendors`): one per vendor (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Meta, xAI, ...), each on or off with a subscription mode (a native CLI login: Claude Code, Codex) and an API mode (an API key); a registry provider runs while its vendor and mode are on (`models/vendors.ts`). Pre-vendor `providers` settings migrate on load
- This Foundry's name (`installationName`), which Kingdom pairing uses
- Agent definitions (id, kind, prompt, provider, model, temperature, visible/owned layers). No Wardens: a `domain-advising`, `domain-librarian` or `decider` agent in `agents` or `projects[id].agents` is refused by name (`refuseHandNamedWardens`), with the fix
- The composition view (`composition`): the instruction ladder and what each role picks from it
- Layer definitions (id, maxTokens, sources)
- Data sources
- Project settings

The viewer dashboard reads and writes this config. `ConfigStore` handles persistence with JSON patch semantics.

A Warden is three parts: **instructions** and **domain knowledge**, both composed by the composition view, and **thread knowledge**, generated per thread by its post-work review. The composition view is one ladder that composes every slot for every role, main thread included ([usage-and-context.md](docs/usage-and-context.md), "Composition view"). Instructions are the generated agent's `prompt` (the generic region instructions plus its region's title and routing line) plus the ladder's files for its role. Domain knowledge is its region's knowledge.md (a generated `domainKnowledge` source) plus the role's files and the general files (CLAUDE.md and the like) of the nodes its `general` names. Both live in private layers, never on the thread's stack, and a Warden owns no configured layer. Each phase (advise, guard, review) appends its own response protocol, so a Warden prompt never states a JSON shape. Every Warden classifies through `@inixiative/foundry/classify` (`packages/foundry/src/classify/`), Foundry's one classification primitive, the same code live, in the evals and in Oracle's experiments: a run of at most three stages (`chorus.wardens.stages`; default one stage, today's Warden), each naming its model and effort, the region doc it reads, its outcomes (binary or ternary), its reason (none, inline, followup), its task (recognise or point) and what it escalates. A pointing stage runs under the fixed Warden charter (`WARDEN_CHARTER`, `classify/charters/point.warden.ts`, composed above its instructions, never settings: point only, the main thread decides), a recognising stage under the recognise charter; charters are Foundry's per task and role, and refused in settings (each is named sections in committed files, `classify/charters/<prompt>/<section>.md`, which only an eval run's `sections` may set; a stage's modes, ternary or a why inline or asked after, add their own sections from `classify/charters/<prompt>/modes/<mode>/<name>.md`, each placed `after` a section or at the end, or, as an explicit dagger, `overrides` one, sent unless its file says `enabled: false`; the assembler itself holds no mode text). Each stage's response protocol is generated from it (the default is exactly the advice and guard protocols: pointer-only, guard findings advisory with no suggestion) and its answer read strictly, a malformed one counted, never guessed. Every Warden is asked at every trigger point that reaches it (`user-message`; `agent-action`, once per turn over the turn's whole tool activity when it ends, not per tool call, `guard: "per-call"` restoring a guard per call; `subagent-spawn`, a brief when the agent hands a task to a subagent; `consumed`, when the main thread takes in a ticket, spec, Linear issue or Notion page, opt-in per project with `chorus.consumed`) unless the pre-filter (`prefilter`, off by default until a local model clears the bar; a local decision model, failing open) is on and confident the moment is outside its domain; `NO_COMMENT` is the expected answer and adds nothing to the thread ([FLOW.md](docs/FLOW.md#when-a-warden-weighs-in-the-charter-trigger-points-and-no_comment)). A Warden's advice is appended to the user's message as "The <domain> Warden chimed in:"; a handoff brief rides with the parent's next message as "The <domain> Warden chimed in on the handoff to <description>:".

A project's Wardens are its **chorus** (`projects[id].chorus`, over the repository's committed `<project>/.foundry/project.json` `chorus`, the machine's settings winning key by key), opt-in (`"enabled": true`; regions present but not enabled are reported as off), built from its concept regions, `<project>/.foundry/regions/<id>/{region.json,knowledge.md}` (`agents/region-roster.ts`, through `resolveProjectView`): one domain-librarian Warden per region, its knowledge the region's knowledge.md in full, run under the charter (an instruction to build is a reason to look; `NO_COMMENT`, or a pointer, ranked `Look over here: <name> (<where>) — <why>` then `Less likely: …`, an `All of these:` set, or a `Choose one:` sibling set unless a stage turns `pointer.any` off, at most three names; Wardens point, the main thread decides). A region declares its `role` (`warden` by default, or `herald`: the socket only, Heralds are not built and their regions never run); `stages` or `charter` in `region.json` are refused by name. Each stage's doc must be in every region of its role, or the chorus is not built and `view.chorus.missingDocs` names the region and doc; each doc is its own source (`region:<id>`, `region:<id>:<doc>`), version and warm key. A later stage keeps its own primed session (`<thread>:aux:domain:<d>:stage:<n>`) and, on another model or effort, its own decision host; it gets a share of the trigger's deadline, and when it times out, fails or answers out of shape the previous stage's outcome stands, journalled (`classified` on the contribution). Only a pointing stage's yes reaches the thread. Multi-stage is off by default (no project sets stages). Region Wardens are the only Wardens: not enabled, or enabled with no regions, the project has no Wardens and the view says why (`view.chorus`: `on`, `enabled`, `enabledBy`, `reason`); a thread without a project has none. `chorus.source` is refused by name (no alias: `"source": "regions"` is now `"enabled": true`, and `"roster"` has no replacement). A thread of a running chorus holds the reception charter (`CHORUS_RECEPTION`, how to read a chime, including the acknowledgement rule for a system the instruction contradicts) once as a standing layer; `chorus.reception: false` leaves it out. A chorus may be layered (`chorus.layers`, in order: a later layer's region replaces an earlier one whole); each region has a warm-cache key, the content hash of its composed knowledge, journalled with every call (`versions.chorus`). There is no global setting. Org and personal `.foundry/roles/<region id>/` files overlay a region. Feedback routes to the project's region Wardens (`feedback/routing.ts`, `wardenRoles(config, projectId)`). See [usage-and-context.md](docs/usage-and-context.md), "Chorus".

A project agent (`projects[id].agents`, never a Warden) is **standalone** (a full definition) or **`extends: <global agent id>`**. An extension appends its `prompt` (under a heading per chunk) and its `domainKnowledge` (source ids, each under its label) to the parent's, global first; `override: ["instructions" | "domainKnowledge"]` replaces that chunk instead. No entry means the global agent applies unchanged. `GET /api/projects/:id/resolved/agents` shows where each chunk came from.

Settings edits apply live: every committed change is a row in Foundry's audit log, `.foundry/audit.jsonl` (before/after per definition, `GET /api/settings/history`), and running threads take edited layers, agents and Cartographer/Warden instructions on their next turn. Adding or removing a region (or enabling the chorus), and provider changes, apply to new threads.

Every Warden call records what its instructions and domain knowledge were composed from, as version ids, not text (`audit/`, docs/THREAD-TREE.md spec B). The audit log holds a **source version** for every change to a source: a settings definition, a ladder file (`file:<path>`), a settings prompt (`prompt:agent:<id>`), a configured source's text (`source-content:<id>`), a feedback-written line, or the charter. Each row records the actor and the cause. The journal's `composition_version` lists a slot's parts in order (glue, source version plus the text it contributed, per-message text), so `CompositionAuditor.recompose` returns the exact text. Advice, guard and review requests carry `versions: {charter, instructions, domainKnowledge, retrieved?, chorus?}` (`chorus` is a region Warden's region and warm-cache key); text chosen per message is stored raw with the call.

A thread is a tree (docs/THREAD-TREE.md spec A).
- **Subagents.** The executor's native subagents (Claude Agent/Task, Codex sub-agents) are recorded as observed child threads (`turns/subagents.ts`), tied to their real parent by `handoff` / `handoff-return` rows. At the spawn the root thread's Wardens brief the handoff (an `advice` row on the parent, `trigger: subagent-spawn`); in the in-session runtime each subagent turn is guarded once when it ends, on the subagent's node.
- **Compaction.** When a turn closes, each middleware call gets a `middleware-reduced` row: its state (versions) and its result, never its input.
- **Retention.** Raw middleware rows age out after `journal.rawMiddlewareDays` (default 30).
- **Archive.** It gets reduced entries and per-node snapshots with `lineage`. Capture claims the native sessions it records, with a lease, so the Archive collector skips them unless Foundry dies before fulfilling.

<!-- unit doc:docs/SYSTEM.md#6-database-schema-prisma-schema-prisma -->
**Source:** `docs/SYSTEM.md` § 6. Database Schema (`prisma/schema.prisma`) (in "Foundry System Documentation")

#### 6. Database Schema (`prisma/schema.prisma`)

PostgreSQL with pgvector extension.

| Model | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `Entry` | Knowledge units (conventions, corrections, ADRs) with vector embeddings |
| `Trace` | Full span tree as JSONB |
| `Span` | Flattened spans for cross-trace queries |
| `Signal` | Typed side-channel information |
| `Intervention` | Manual operator overrides |
| `ThreadState` | Persisted thread metadata |
| `Message` | Conversation within threads |

- **bun run db:push:test** `package.json` [script] push the Prisma schema to the local foundry_test database Use: bun run db:push:test
